column1: # Stress genes absent from yeast-GEM v9.0.2's 1161-gene list, and what was done about each.
# Absence was established by ORF against the fbc:geneProduct labels in data/gem/yeast-GEM.xml.gz
# (ystwin.fba.stress_genes.gene_label_map), never by symbol: symbols collide. "CTR1" as a bare
# string resolves in SGD to YGL077C (HNM1, choline transporter), which IS in the model; the copper
# transporter CTR1 is YPR124W, which is not. "CRH2" and "UTR2" are one gene, YEL040W. "VMA12" and
# "VPH2" are one gene, YKL119C. "UAP1" is YDL103C, present under its canonical symbol QRI1.
# Every function claim carries a GO molecular-function term and the SGD evidence line behind it,
# Nothing here is asserted without one, and that is enforced rather than promised: every triple
# below is looked up in that GAF by stress_genes.unsupported_claims(), which must come back empty
# and which must match on aspect F. It found one invented citation on its first run -- SMF2's
# manganese term is IBA in SGD, not the IDA this file claimed -- and that row now says IBA.
# Every stoichiometric coefficient below is 1: these are single mannosyl transfers, so there is
# no rate, kcat or yield anywhere in this file to invent.
# The one modelling choice that is ASSERTED rather than cited is MANPOL_G's compartments -- see
# its `basis` -- and it copies the shape yeast-GEM already uses at r_0005 and r_0006.
#   GPR_EXTEND      the reaction exists; only the gene-protein rule was missing or misassigned.
#   NEW_REACTION    the chemistry is genuinely absent; the reaction is added by this module.
#   REFUSED         adding it would be wrong. The reason is in `basis`. This list is the point.
#   ALREADY_PRESENT the brief listed it as absent and it is not. Recorded so nobody re-adds it.
# For GPR_EXTEND, `old_rule` is asserted against the loaded model before `new_rule` replaces it:
# a yeast-GEM whose rule has moved on refuses the edit instead of silently overwriting it.
# For NEW_REACTION, every row on one target must agree on reaction_name/stoichiometry/bounds/new_rule.

column9: new_rule
column12: basis

column9: (YDR453C and YGR209C) or (YDR453C and YLR043C) or (YML028W and YGR209C) or (YML028W and YLR043C)
column12: Thioredoxin peroxidase activity, the exact chemistry of r_0550; the model carries only the minor paralogue TSA2 (YDR453C). Added as a TRX1/TRX2 pair, matching the existing clause shape. MEASURED, through the repo's own gene-level layer: at oxidative activity +0.5 bridge/regulation.eflux_layer scales r_0550 by 1.000 without this row and 1.500 with it (upper bound 1000 -> 1500 mmol/gDCW/h), because YAP1/SKN7's regulon names TSA1 and TRX2 but not TSA2. That is the false negative in one number.

column9: YDR456W or YJL129C or YKR050W
column12: Potassium ion transmembrane transporter; the second half of the Trk1p-Trk2p system whose Trk1 (YJL129C) already carries r_1249.

column9: (YMR058W and YER145C) or YMR319C
column12: Ferrous iron transporter; SGD qualifies a second annotation contributes_to (PMID:16700543), i.e. a complex subunit, so it joins FET3 with AND. FET4 (YMR319C) stays an independent low-affinity route. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, measured: an AND costs reach when a regulon names only one subunit. At hypoxia +0.5, whose regulon names FET3 and not FTR1, r_1178's E-Flux scale falls from 1.500 to 1.000. The iron and copper regulons name FTR1 and not FET3, so they did not reach r_1178 at all before this row and scale it 1.000 after -- against a reference capacity of 1000, which is the reaction's own upper bound, so no bound moves either way. A complex is limited by its scarcest subunit, so the partial regulon is the gap, not the AND.

column9: YOL122C or YPR124W or YLR411W
column12: Copper ion transmembrane transporter. r_4589 carried only SMF1 (YOL122C), whose own annotated function is manganese transport (GO:0005384), so copper uptake had no correct gene at all. MEASURED: at copper activity +0.5 the CUP2/MAC1 regulon reaches r_4589 not at all without this row and scales it by 1.500 with it; the same two genes are in the AFT1/AFT2 iron regulon.

column9: YOL122C or YPR124W or YLR411W
column12: Second high-affinity copper transporter, independent of CTR1, hence OR.

column9: YOL130W or YHR050W
column12: Manganese transporter. r_4590 carried only ALR1 (YOL130W), whose annotated function is magnesium transport (GO:0015095), so alr1 deletion wrongly removed the cell's only manganese supply. EVIDENCE IS PHYLOGENETIC, and it is recorded as such: SGD's only aspect-F line for the manganese-specific term GO:0005384 on this ORF is IBA. The experimental support is one level less specific on each side -- GO:0022857 transmembrane transporter activity, IDA:PMID:10574989, and the process term GO:0006828 manganese ion transport, IMP:PMID:11602606.

column9: YOL122C or (YGR217W and YNL291C)
column12: Calcium channel activity. r_4587 carried only SMF1, a manganese transporter. Mid1p works only with Cch1p, so the clause is an AND.

column9: YOL122C or (YGR217W and YNL291C)
column12: Obligate partner of MID1 in the high-affinity calcium influx system; the same paper annotates both. Introduced with MID1 rather than alone.

column9: (YPL050C and YML115C) or (YPL050C and YEL036C and YDR245W and YJL183W) or YER001W or YBR015C or YJL186W or YGL257C or YIL014W
column12: Alpha-1,6-mannosyltransferase, qualified contributes_to: a subunit of mannan polymerase I (with VAN1) and II (with ANP1/MNN10/MNN11), hence the two AND clauses. Yeast-GEM's only route to the 0.70204 mmol/gDCW mannan in r_4048 was Dol-P-Man via PMT (r_0362); the GDP-mannose route that builds the outer chain was missing entirely. ASSERTED compartments: the reaction draws GDP-mannose from [g] and leaves GDP and H+ there, but deposits the mannan repeat unit in [c], because yeast-GEM has no mannan species in [g]. That is the same shape as the model's own cell-wall synthases r_0005 and r_0006, which each consume UDP-D-glucose in [c] and deposit the beta-glucan in [ce] in one step. (r_0272, chitin synthase, is the same reaction shape but stays within [c], so it is a weaker precedent and is named here only for completeness.) Writing it in [er] instead was tried and measured at FVA [0, 0]: GDP-mannose[er] and GDP[er] have no transport in or out, so the model's whole ER glycosylation module is an unfed fragment. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, measured: adding this route flips DPM1 (YPR183W) from 0.000000 to 0.085844 /h on deletion. DPM1 is essential in reality, and it was essential in yeast-GEM only because r_0362 was the sole mannan producer. Its real reason for being essential -- GPI anchoring and protein O-mannosylation -- cannot make it essential here, because the model's GPI-anchor and N-glycan branches both dead-end. That gap is upstream of this row and is not repaired by it.

column12: Alpha-1,3-mannosyltransferase acting alone on the same outer chain. In a lumped mannan repeat unit every GDP-mannose-dependent transfer onto the chain is one and the same reaction, so backbone and branch enzymes share it; the linkage distinction is not representable here and is not claimed. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, measured: MNN1 is the only gene on this reaction that any module regulon names, so MANPOL_G enters the E-Flux layer of the cell_wall and oxidative modules and is scaled 1.500 at activity +0.5, lifting its upper bound 1000 -> 1500. That is inert -- FVA puts the reaction's own maximum at 0.060266 mmol/gDCW/h under the shipped default bounds -- but it is a bound this module moves and it is declared here rather than found later.

column9: YBL082C
column12: The exact missing bridge between yeast-GEM's two disconnected halves of the dolichol N-glycan chain. s_3989 (Man5) ran only to s_3990 (G00006), which has exactly one reaction and so is a dead end; s_3993 (Man6) appears in exactly one reaction, r_4313, and only as a substrate, so nothing produces it in the biosynthetic direction. One mannosyl unit, C6H10O5, transferred from Dol-P-Man. NOTE: the whole branch is blocked downstream -- it terminates at s_3887 with no oligosaccharyltransferase -- so this reaction is exact but carries zero flux until that separate gap is closed.
Protein-macromolecule adaptor activity and nothing else: a scaffold tethering Erg25/Erg26/Erg27. It catalyses no reaction, so it belongs in no GPR.
Heme binding is its only annotated molecular function. A regulatory heme-binding protein supporting Erg11, not an enzyme.
Superoxide dismutase copper chaperone activity: it delivers a metal to Sod1p and turns over no metabolite.
V-ATPase assembly factor. SGD assigns it the root molecular_function term with evidence code ND -- no function known. Also the same gene as VMA12; the brief's two names are one ORF.
V-ATPase assembly factor; root molecular_function, evidence ND. Not an enzyme, and r_1086 already carries the sixteen genuine V-ATPase subunits.
Protein binding only. V-ATPase assembly factor, not a subunit and not a catalyst.
Enzyme activator activity: a positive regulator of the mannosylphosphate transferase Ktr6/Mnn6, which the model already has on r_0192. A regulator is not a catalyst.

Electron transfer activity, no catalytic annotation. Yeast-GEM writes the sterol desaturations (r_0242, r_0233) with NADPH as the direct donor, so no reaction carries its chemistry; making it an obligate AND partner would predict cyb5 deletion blocks ergosterol, which is false.

1,4-alpha-glucan branching enzyme. Glycogen is one lumped repeat unit in this model (s_0773, C6H10O5); branching rearranges bonds without changing that unit, so the reaction would be substrate equals product.

1,3-beta-glucanosyltransferase. Both substrate and product are the model's single lumped (1->3)-beta-D-glucan repeat unit (s_0001/s_0002, C6H10O5), so the reaction is the identity. Unrepresentable, not missing.
Same chemistry and same lumped-polymer obstruction as GAS1.

Same chemistry and same lumped-polymer obstruction as GAS1.
Chitin-glucan transglycosylase. Chitin (s_0509) and beta-glucan (s_0001/s_0004) are lumped repeat units, so cross-linking one to the other moves no atoms in this representation.
Same as CRH1. This ORF is also the brief's CRH2; the two names are one gene.

Outward-rectifying potassium channel. REFUSED BY MEASUREMENT, and the earlier argued reason was wrong. The K+ efflux reaction it needs (s_1373 --> s_1374, bounds 0,1000) was added and measured: growth 0.085844 /h under the shipped default bounds, 77.556090 /h with every exchange open, max ATP per glucose 19.192 mmol/mmol, and a closed medium still drains no ATP -- every number identical to the model without it. The proton cycle it looks like it would open is already open: r_2020 (K+ exchange) and r_1832 (H+ exchange) are both (-1000, 1000), so r_1249 can already carry protons inward against nothing, with or without this channel. It is refused because it moves no number, not because it would be a free lunch.
Potassium:proton antiporter of the Golgi. The model has potassium in c, e and v only -- there is no potassium species in [g] to move.
Calcium:proton antiporter of the ER. The model has Ca(2+) in c, v, g and e only -- there is no Ca(2+) in [er].

Vacuolar calcium:proton antiporter, and it moves calcium the same way r_4237 (PMC1) does, into the vacuole. Ca(2+)[v] (s_3882) has no efflux at all, so r_4237 already measures [0, 0] under FVA and any further importer would too. The gap is a missing vacuolar calcium exit, not a missing entry.
The brief listed this ORF as absent under the alias UAP1. It is in yeast-GEM under its canonical symbol QRI1, carrying r_1069, UDP-N-acetylglucosamine diphosphorylase. Nothing to add.
The brief's MNN6 is this ORF. It is in yeast-GEM as KTR6 on r_0192, alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase. Nothing to add.
